institution: Sorbonne Université (Faculté des Sciences et Ingénierie), in collaboration with IRCAM and Télécom Paris
programme: M2 ATIAM — Acoustique, Traitement du signal, Informatique, Appliqués à la Musique
stillExists: YES. Running and recruiting. The application page publishes a live calendar for the 2026-2027 intake (application window 26 March – 11 June 2026, results by July, start early September 2026). No sign of discontinuation.
awards: A real second-cycle degree — but only the SECOND YEAR of one. ATIAM is an M2 (fifth year) within Sorbonne Université's national master's. Sorbonne Université's own fee page states the master's rate: "For master's degree programmes, the tuition fee is €255 for the 2026-2027 academic year." The diploma is the French Diplôme National de Master.
acceptsSoftwareEngineeringBachelor: NO — not at this level. The page requires an already-completed FIRST year of a master's: "niveau de maîtrise ou master M1 en informatique ou mathématiques" (for the IT profile) or "master 1 en physique/acoustique" (for the acoustics/signal profile). Engineering-school diploma holders (diplôme d'ingénieur, bac+5) are also eligible. A three-year BSc is bac+3 and is two years short.
liveAudition: NO live audition. The gate is (1) a dossier via Sorbonne's eCandidat and (2) "Entretien de motivation" — a motivation interview held at IRCAM. It is an academic interview, not a performance audition and not a portfolio review. But it probes signal-processing/CS competence at M1 level.
portfolioSpec: There is NO artistic portfolio requirement. The dossier is academic: transcripts, CV, a motivation letter that must explicitly state interest in ATIAM, and optional recommendation letters. Selection criteria quoted: "un niveau similaire à celui atteint à l'issue d'une première année de master" in one or two of the core subjects, plus motivation/musical interest and "un bon niveau d'anglais."
costForTunisian: Sorbonne Université national master rate 255 €/yr (verified on the university's own enrolment page). Differentiated fees (droits différenciés) DO formally apply to non-EU students — Sorbonne's page confirms it applies them — but the same page describes automatic full exemptions and an Exemption Committee route. Press reporting (12 July 2026) says the Sorbonne CA voted unanimously on 7 July 2026 to exonerate all non-EU students so they pay the same as everyone else; the exact differentiated master figure (reported around 3 941 €) is NOT published on Sorbonne's own English fee page — UNVERIFIED on an official page. CVEC is compulsory and paid to CROUS; the amount is not published on that page.
funding: Nothing programme-specific published on the ATIAM candidature page. UNVERIFIED — no ATIAM-run scholarship found. Tunisians would depend on the French Embassy/Campus France BGF (Bourse du Gouvernement Français), which is a separate, earlier application, not automatic on admission.
applicationDeadline: 2026-2027 cycle (PRIOR CYCLE, use as the pattern): applications 26 March – 11 June 2026; interviews at IRCAM (date TBA); results by July; enrolment July–October; start early September. Expect the same March–June window in 2027. IMPORTANT for Tunisia: a Tunisian resident applying to a first enrolment in a French institution must go through Campus France Tunisie / Études en France, whose 'Ne t'arrête pas' cycle typically opens the previous autumn (Oct–Dec) and closes well before the university's own June date — the Études en France dossier is the real binding deadline.
languageOfInstruction: French. "Les cours sont en majorité dispensés en français" — a good level of French is recommended for non-francophones. "Un bon niveau d'anglais" is also a selection criterion. No specific certificate named on this page.
verdictWhy: He is structurally ineligible: ATIAM is an M2 that starts from a completed M1 or a five-year engineering diploma, and he has a three-year BSc. Even if he closed that gap, ATIAM is a hard signal-processing/acoustics research master, not an artist-development programme — it would not build him a career as an electronic music producer. Do not spend an application on it.
correction: The input row implies this is an entry-level master reachable with 'Portfolio only'. Both are wrong. (a) There is NO portfolio at all — the gate is an academic dossier plus a motivation interview. (b) It is an M2 requiring bac+4 (M1 completed), not a two-year master a BSc holder can enter. (c) Cost band 'EUR 1.5k-5k/yr' is misleading: the published Sorbonne master rate is 255 €/yr, and non-EU differentiated fees are subject to a Sorbonne exemption policy.

stillExists: YES. Programme page live, winter-semester start, structure "4 Semester" plus "1 Diplomsemester".
awards: NOT A MASTER'S DEGREE. It awards a "Diplom der Filmakademie Baden-Württemberg" — an institutional diploma from a state film academy, classified as a "Diplomaufbaustudium" (postgraduate diploma course). It is not an accredited second-cycle Bologna master's and carries no ECTS-bearing MA/MFA title. This matters for a student visa and for any later PhD or academic route.
acceptsSoftwareEngineeringBachelor: CASE-BY-CASE but effectively hostile. The formal entry is a Hochschulzugangsberechtigung ("Sollten Sie keine Allgemeine Hochschulreife/Abitur vorweisen können, gibt es die Möglichkeit, den Zugang … über den sogenannten Begabtenpassus … zu erlangen"). For the postgraduate/Projektstudium route applicants need a prior degree OR substantial professional media experience. The real filter is craft: "Grundkenntnisse in Tonstudiotechnik" and "Arbeitsumgang mit Digital Audio Workstations (DAW)" are demanded.
liveAudition: YES — a multi-stage in-person entrance examination (Aufnahmeprüfung), and it is decisive. The published process: "Einzelgespräche mit den leitenden Dozierenden der jeweiligen Abteilung, die Ausgabe der 72-Stunden-Prüfungsaufgabe sowie das abschließende Gespräch innerhalb des Kolloquiums" — individual interviews with department heads, a 72-hour set practical exam task, and a concluding colloquium. It is not a music audition but it is a live, timed, in-person practical test he cannot bluff.
portfolioSpec: Not published on the pages reached. Work samples are requested inside the online application form. UNVERIFIED — I could not find a page specifying number of works, length or format for Filmton/Sounddesign; the decisive assessed artefact is the 72-hour exam task, not a prior portfolio.
costForTunisian: "1.500€ (Nicht-EU-Bürger)" per year for non-EU citizens (EU students pay €0 for this postgraduate course). Additional semester contributions, Studentenwerk and the compulsory German student health insurance (statutory student rate, roughly €130+/month, amount not published by the academy) are not itemised on the page — UNVERIFIED. Blocked-account proof for the German visa is a separate, much larger requirement.
funding: No programme scholarship published on the reached pages. Input claims 'Partial' — UNVERIFIED; I found no named Filmakademie scholarship for this course. German external routes (DAAD) would be a separate, earlier application, and DAAD study scholarships generally target accredited degree programmes, which this is not.
applicationDeadline: "Bewerbungsfrist ist der 15. Februar" — 15 February each year, for the following winter semester. So for an autumn-2027 start: 15 February 2027. This is a stable recurring pattern (only Motion Design differs, 15 May).
languageOfInstruction: German, with some English: "Deutsch/Englisch im PS". German is required at "Goethe Institut Level B2" (or TestDaF 4 / DSH-2). He has NO German.
verdictWhy: Three independent blockers, any one of which is fatal: it demands German at B2 and he has none; it ends in a Filmakademie Diplom rather than a recognised master's degree; and admission runs through an in-person multi-day entrance exam including a 72-hour practical task that assumes existing studio and DAW craft. It is also film post-production, not electronic music.
correction: DEGREE TYPE: the input treats this as a master-level option. It is not a master's — it awards a "Diplom der Filmakademie Baden-Württemberg" from a Diplomaufbaustudium, not an accredited second-cycle degree. GATE: 'Exam/interview only' understates it — the exam includes a 72-hour set practical task plus a colloquium, in person. LANGUAGE: German B2 (Goethe B2 / TestDaF 4 / DSH-2) is required and is not flagged in the input.

institution: Liszt Ferenc Zeneművészeti Egyetem (Liszt Academy of Music), Composition Department
programme: Music Composition MA — Electroacoustic Composition specialisation
stillExists: YES. The MA Composition requirements page is live and the electroacoustic specialisation has its own published exam list. Applications for the 2026 intake are open; entrance exams for 2026 were held in person in Budapest in June 2026.
awards: A real second-cycle MA in Music (Composition), 4 semesters, from a state-recognised Hungarian university of music. Not a certificate.
acceptsSoftwareEngineeringBachelor: NO in practice. The requirements page states no explicit prior-degree field, but the entrance exam presupposes conservatoire-level training: it demands "Analysis of a 20th-century instrumental, and an electroacoustic composition (or excerpt)", "Analysis of a contemporary graphic music notation", "The basics of electronic music: test", plus a MIDI-sequencer orchestration of chamber music. A software-engineering graduate with no music theory cannot sit this.
liveAudition: YES in substance — a multi-part in-person entrance examination in Budapest, not a portfolio review. Published components include written analysis exams, an oral component, a computer-based practical task ("The basics of electronic music: a practical task to be completed on a computer") and MIDI orchestration. For the 2026 cycle the exams took place in person in Budapest in June 2026. It is an exam, not a stage performance, but it is live, timed and theory-heavy.
portfolioSpec: PRECISE AND PUBLISHED. Submit: "Presentation of a fixed electroacoustic music piece and another piece applying live electronics with an acoustic instrument" — i.e. two works, one fixed-media and one live-electronics-with-acoustic-instrument. Total duration cap: "The pieces submitted together must not exceed 25-30 minutes." PLUS two style exercises: "1 short etude in the style of any significant 20th-century musique concrète composer" and "1 short etude in the style of significant 20th-century synthesis technique composer". Format not specified on the page.
costForTunisian: Liszt Academy's own fee table: "950,000 HUF per semester" for non-EU international students on all master's training programmes = 1,900,000 HUF/year (roughly EUR 4,700–5,000 at 2026 rates; the Academy notes payment may be made in EUR at the MNB rate on the first day of classes). Application fee and entrance-exam fee are NOT published on the fee page — UNVERIFIED. Hungarian student residence permit requires separate proof of maintenance.
funding: UNVERIFIED for this candidate. The Academy's application page lists Erasmus and CEEPUS (mobility, not degree funding) and no deadlines. Stipendium Hungaricum is the realistic route for a Tunisian, but it is a bilateral government scheme requiring Tunisia to be a partner country and it is a separate, earlier application (typically closing in January) — I could not confirm Tunisia's current eligibility on an official page. No automatic-on-admission funding published.
applicationDeadline: PRIOR CYCLE: the Academy publishes "Application deadline: 31 March (every year)" for non-degree programmes; for full-time degree programmes the 2026 pattern was admission requirements published December 2025, entrance exams in person in Budapest in June 2026. Expect the same December-publication / spring-deadline / June-exam rhythm for a September 2027 start. Exact 2027 dates not yet published.
languageOfInstruction: Hungarian by default. Critical caveat quoted from the requirements page: "Tuition is only offered in English if there are a minimum of 3 international students admitted in a given year to the same major." So English teaching is conditional on cohort composition, not guaranteed. No English certificate level published on the pages reached.
verdictWhy: The entrance exam is a conservatoire theory exam — analysis of 20th-century instrumental and electroacoustic scores, graphic notation, MIDI orchestration of chamber music — plus two stylistic etudes in musique concrete and classic synthesis. That is three or four years of training he does not have and cannot fake by 2027. English teaching is also not guaranteed unless three internationals happen to enrol in the same major.
correction: LANGUAGE: the input does not flag that English instruction is conditional — "Tuition is only offered in English if there are a minimum of 3 international students admitted in a given year to the same major." COST: input band 'EUR 1.5k-5k/yr'; the published non-EU rate is 950,000 HUF per semester (1.9m HUF/yr), which sits at or just above the top of that band depending on the exchange rate. GATE: 'Portfolio + exam/interview' understates the exam — it is a written and practical music-theory examination, not an interview.
